title: On the Computational Complexity of Hidden Markov Model Identification
summary: Identification is the task of recovering the parameters of an unknown ground-truth model from sampled data. When parameters other than the ground truth induce the same output distribution, data alone does not provide enough information to recover the ground truth, and the model is thus called unidentifiable. We study the identifiability problem for hidden Markov models (HMMs): given an HMM, is it identifiable? Existing work on HMM identification establishes conditions under which the ground-truth HMM can be identified. However, most of these conditions are sufficient but not necessary,…
